front.title: Effect Acknowledgement for HTTP and Web Linking

abstract.t: This document defines an Experimental HTTP binding for the QIK-VRT Effect Acknowledgement protocol. It introduces two Structured Fields and a Web Linking relation for capability discovery, preparation of a protected effect, validation of a full responsibility record, and exact-bound commit.

Revision -01 makes explicit that protocol sequence is not itself evidence of causality. A protected effect is released only from explicitly bound authority, evidence and causal dependencies; serialization is an implementation projection of that causal structure.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: HTTP success, transport acknowledgement, successful parsing and application return values do not establish authorization for an external effect. The EFFECT_ACK core protocol separates those concepts. This document maps that gate to HTTP without changing HTTP method semantics.
The binding uses Structured Field Values for HTTP and Web Linking . The same link relation can be represented in the HTTP Link field or by an HTML link element.

section.name: Conventions and Requirements
section.t: The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED, NOT RECOMMENDED, MAY, and OPTIONAL are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals.

This document assumes the five-state EFFECT_ACK model: EFFECT_NACK, EFFECT_ACK_CONTINUE, EFFECT_ACK_DONE, EFFECT_ACK_ISOLATE and EFFECT_ACK_BLOCK. Only a fresh, authenticated and independently validated EFFECT_ACK_DONE record can be eligible for ordinary release.

section.name: Causality, Serialization and Metagrammar Binding
section.t: An implementation MUST NOT infer causal authorization from message order, wall-clock order, source-text order, transport completion, or a successful status code alone. Sequence can record order; it is not by itself proof of a causal dependency or authority.

A deployment that represents protected work as a directed causal graph MAY serialize causally independent operations in any deterministic topological order consistent with the explicit dependency edges. Parallel or distributed execution MAY use another topological projection of the same graph. Such projection MUST preserve all bound non-commutative effects, authority constraints, lease constraints, exact-version constraints and Effect-Ack dependencies.

Where a deployment uses a QIK-VRT metagrammar envelope, the responsibility-record digest SHOULD bind canonical bytes for operation identifier, resource binding, exact version identifiers, intent, authority, evidence, state, effect, next action and proof. Generic HTTP implementations are not required to understand that metagrammar.

A DONE result obtained before execution is an authorization-state record, not post-effect evidence. After a protected effect, a deployment claiming observed completion MUST obtain a distinct post-effect observation. Transport acknowledgement MUST NOT be substituted for that observation.

section.name: Capability Discovery
section.t: An origin supporting this profile SHOULD advertise an effect-ack link relation. Discovery is metadata only and never authorizes an effect.
A fail-closed client MUST establish support before sending a protected operation in prepare mode.

section.name: Effect-Ack-Request Field
section.t: Effect-Ack-Request is a Structured Dictionary. Version 1 defines v (Integer), mode (Token: prepare or commit), token (Byte Sequence, required for commit), and hash (Byte Sequence, the SHA-256 digest of the canonical responsibility record, required for commit).
section.sourcecode: Effect-Ack-Request: v=1, mode=prepare Effect-Ack-Request: v=1, mode=commit, token=:AQIDBAUGBwgJCgsMDQ4PEA==:, hash=:AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=:
section.t: A server receiving prepare MUST NOT execute the protected effect.

section.name: Effect-Ack Field
section.t: Effect-Ack is a Structured Dictionary. Version 1 defines v, state (nack, continue, done, isolate or block), hash, and an optional single-use token.
The compact field does not replace the full responsibility record. A consumer MUST obtain and independently validate the exact record before commit.

ol.li: The client discovers the profile and classifies the proposed operation as protected.
The client sends the exact proposed operation with mode=prepare; the protected effect MUST NOT occur.
The server evaluates the request. A non-DONE result does not release the effect.
For DONE the server MAY issue a short-lived single-use token bound to effective request target, method, request-content digest, policy digest, responsible principal, record hash and expiration.
The client independently validates the full responsibility record.
The client repeats the exact operation with mode=commit, token and record hash.
The server atomically revalidates freshness, single use, request equivalence, policy, record integrity and DONE state. Only then MAY the effect occur.
After execution, the deployment SHOULD expose a post-effect observation bound to the actual resulting state. A successful HTTP response alone is not post-effect proof.

section.name: Backward Compatibility and HTML Integration
section.t: The extension is opt-in. Generic recipients can ignore unknown fields. A fail-closed client MUST NOT send a protected operation merely hoping the extension will be understood.
No new HTML element or parser behavior is defined. Ordinary HTML link can express the effect-ack relation. Its presence is discovery evidence only and MUST NOT be interpreted as DONE.

section.name: Browser and Terminal Considerations
section.t: A browser extension can discover the link relation, keep protected requests in prepare state, validate a returned record, and issue commit only after DONE.

Audio, video and screen capture remain Web-platform permission events. Media MUST NOT be silently captured or transmitted, and local preview, submitted input, prepared effect and committed effect MUST remain distinguishable.

A terminal reflecting observations back into an autonomous system MUST treat reflection as input evidence, not implicit authority. Any new productive action begins a new protected operation and Effect-Ack lifecycle.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Threats include forged DONE assertions, token theft, replay, request substitution, downgrade, stale record reuse, policy substitution, alternate-path bypass, confused deputies and compromised evaluators. Commit tokens MUST be unguessable, single-use, short-lived and exact-request bound. HTTP Message Signatures MAY be used to bind relevant HTTP components.

section.name: Privacy Considerations
section.t: Responsibility records can expose principals, policy identifiers and evidence references. Implementations SHOULD minimize metadata and retain media locally until explicit submission.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: IANA is requested to add provisional HTTP Field Name registrations for Effect-Ack and Effect-Ack-Request, both Structured Dictionaries, and to register the Web Link relation effect-ack for an endpoint or representation exposing EFFECT_ACK capability information or a responsibility record bound to the link context.
